nodes.name: Oxidation to Cu(OH)₂ NAs
nodes.procedure: The commercial CF was cut into a rectangular shape with the size of 1.0 × 3.0 cm². Then the small pieces of CF were carefully washed with 3.0 M acid, acetone, and deionized (DI) water, respectively. NaOH (3.0 g) and 0.68 g (NH₄)₂S₂O₈ were dissolved in 30 mL DI water under vigorous stirring and the precleaned Cu substrate was immersed in it. After 20 min, a blue hydroxide layer was observed on the surface of Cu. The Cu substrate covered with nanowires was taken out from the solution and repeatedly rinsed with DI water, and then dried at room temperature.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal sulfidation to CuS NAs
nodes.procedure: Thiourea (0.22 g) was dissolved into 30 mL ethylene glycol under magnetic stirring at room temperature. Then, the solution was loaded into a 50 ml Teflon-lined autoclave and a piece of freshly treated CF supporting Cu(OH)₂ NAs was also added into the autoclave, sealed, heated to 80 °C, and kept at this temperature for 60 min. After the reaction cooled down naturally, the CF with products on it was taken out, washed with water, and dried naturally.

nodes.name: In situ electroreduction to Cu-S NSs
nodes.procedure: The electroreduction of CuS NAs was conducted on an Ivium-n-Stat electrochemical workstation in a typical three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH. A Hg/HgO with 1.0 M KOH as the inner reference electrolyte was used as the reference electrode. A carbon rod was used as the counter-electrode. CuS NAs/CF was in advance sealed with epoxy, to ensure the exposed area of 1.0 cm², and then used as the working electrode. The LSV was recorded in the voltage range -0.7 ~ -1.5 V vs. Hg/HgO at the scan rate of 5 mV s⁻¹ until the reductive peaks disappeared.

nodes.name: In situ electroreduction of Cu(OH)₂ NAs
nodes.procedure: Cu(OH)₂-derived Cu NAs were synthesized by a similar in situ electroreduction strategy to those of Cu-S NSs, where CuS NAs were replaced by Cu(OH)₂ NAs. The electroreduction was conducted in 1.0 M KOH with a three-electrode system using Hg/HgO reference electrode and carbon rod counter-electrode. LSV was recorded until complete reduction.

nodes.name: Cu-S NSs
aliases: surface sulfur-doped and -adsorbed low-coordinated copper nanowire sponges

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show CuS nanowires assembled by small nanoparticles directly grown on copper foam, transforming to nanowire sponges after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (Fig. 2d and Supplementary Figs. 2a–c) showed that CuS nanowires assembled by small nanoparticles were directly grown on a copper foam (CF).

properties.description: Restructured porous material with denser morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows lattice fringes with interplanar distance of 0.305 nm attributed to (102) planes of CuS; HRTEM confirms Cu2O phase with 0.24 nm lattice spacing after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes with an interplanar distance of 0.305 nm in the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image (Supplementary Fig. 2d) were attributed to the (102) planes of CuS.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms hexagonal CuS structure (JCPDS No. 06-0464); after electroreduction shows Cu2O phase; in situ XRD reveals phase transformation CuS → Cu8S5 → Cu2S → Cu with characteristic peaks at 43.3° and 50.6° for Cu(111) and (200).
nodes.evidence_snippet: All the diffraction peaks in the XRD pattern (Fig. 2c) could be indexed to the hexagonal structure of CuS (JCPDS No. 06-0464).

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with multiple peaks labeled at specific 2θ angles

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows clear fringes with lattice spacing of 0.24 nm confirming Cu2O phase after electroreduction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clear fringes with a lattice spacing of 0.24 nm in the HRTEM image also confirmed the Cu2O phase (Supplementary Fig. 5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform Cu and S distribution in CuS NAs; sulfur content in Cu-S NSs is about 5.5 at%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) data suggested the sulfur content of the Cu-S NSs was about 5.5%, implying the severe leaching of sulfur during the reduction process.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of CuS NAs shows Cu 2p3/2 at 932.8 eV (Cu2+), S 2p3/2 at 163.5 eV and S 2p1/2 at 162.3 eV (S2-), atomic % S = 42%; Cu-S NSs shows S decreased to 4.6% with S2- at 163/162 eV, oxidized S at 168 eV, Cu+ at 932.8/953.8 eV (Cu2O), minor Cu2+ at 954.1/934.6 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The prominent peaks at 932.8 eV (Cu 2p3/2) and 952.8 eV (Cu 2p1/2) in the X-ray photoelectron spectra belonged to Cu2+, whereas the characteristic signals at 163.5 eV (S 2p3/2) and 162.3 eV (S 2p1/2) were assigned to S2- (Supplementary Figs. 2e and 3). After the electroreduction conversion, the atomic percentage of sulfur decreased from 42% to 4.6%, in accordance with the EDS results.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ potential-dependent XRD monitors phase transformation: CuS peaks at 48.1° and 59.2° disappear; Cu8S5 peak at 47.5° appears at -0.85 V; Cu2S peaks at 46.0°, 48.3°, 53.9° at -1.0 V; Cu(111) at 43.3° and (200) at 50.6° appear at -1.2 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: First, potential-dependent XRD was used to monitor the phase transformation of the sample (Fig. 3a). ... Thus, these XRD analyses suggested the reduced conversion process of CuS → Cu8S5 → Cu2S → Cu.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows S–S bond vibration of CuS at 472 cm⁻¹ decreases and disappears at -1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO, confirming isolated surface sulfur indicating S-doping and adsorption on Cu.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3b depicted that the S–S bond vibration of CuS at 472 cm⁻¹ decreased gradually with decreasing the applied potential and completely disappeared at -1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Cu K-edge XANES of Cu-S NSs at -1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO similar to Cu foil but absorption edge between Cu2S and Cu; EXAFS shows Cu-Cu bonds at 2.3 Å and Cu-S bonds at 1.8 Å, confirming surface sulfur and low-coordinated Cu atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cu K-edge extended X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra (XANES) and the corresponding derivative curves of Cu-S NSs at -1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO both exhibited similar features to Cu foil (Fig. 3c and Supplementary Fig. 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV curves during electroreduction show three reduction peaks at -0.8 V, -1.05 V, and -1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO corresponding to CuS/Cu8S5, Cu8S5/Cu2S, and Cu2S/Cu reductions respectively; peaks fade and vanish by fourth scan.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves showed three typical reduction peaks at −0.8, −1.05, and −1.3 V vs. Hg/HgO corresponding to the reduction of CuS/Cu8S5, Cu8S5/Cu2S, and Cu2S/Cu, respectively.
